description: I’m Arin, a PhD student with experience in signal processing and satellite data products. I’m looking for teammates who enjoy geospatial analysis and data visualization. If that sounds like you, I’d love to team up for building our Space Apps project together.
summary:
FlareFront is an interactive web application that is built to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS hotspot counts into a historical record of fire activity. It uses NASA FIRMS observations from 2001-2025 to calculate county specific scaling factors from overlapping Terra MODIS and Suomi-NPP VIIRS records for making detection counts more comparable across sensors. Users of this platform can explore fire calendars and hotspot maps, switch between raw and harmonized counts, examine seasonal patterns and download data.

The website also includes a real case study across five California counties, which demonstrated that calibrated VIIRS counts had lower monthly error when compared against Terra than both raw VIIRS counts and seasonal baseline as an indicator of improved sensor count agreement.

FlareFront addresses the MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots Challenge by connecting transparent harmonization with accessible visual exploration tools to help users of the platform distinguish sensor differences from historical patterns and unusually active periods while giving them the ability to export and download data.
details:
FlareFront harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS hotspot counts to help its users explore historical fire activity, seasonal patterns and unusually active years through tools such as fire calendars and hotspot maps. It calibrates VIIRS counts to Terra MODIS through NASA FIRMS observations using 2013-2019 data and evaluates agreement during 2020-2025. The calibrated counts reduced monthly error against Terra compared with raw VIIRS and a seasonal baseline across 5 selected California counties.

FlareFront connects transparent calibration with geographic exploration through tools such as interactive calendars, maps, and comparison plots while also enabling downloading data and plots. It is built with Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, and uses Plotly.js, Leaflet, Census TIGERweb boundaries and OpenStreetMap. GitHub and Cloudflare Pages are used for hosting and delivery of this project. An AI/SI-assisted code editor (VS Code) was used for editing, debugging, and documenting the code used in this project.

The project presents exploratory results demonstrating improved monthly satellite count agreement, while raw observations remain available, and the custom areas retains uncalibrated counts.
